annotations.annotation_text: Page 102 opens Book 1, Chapter 4 ("The Burial of HCE") during the Age of Gods (transition) phase. This passage continues the burial of the giant in the landscape, the archaeological mound, the Four Annalists surveying history, featuring HCE, Mamalujo, Kate the Slop. The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.

annotations.annotation_text: ALP invocation "A.L.P" on page 102 ("The Burial of HCE"): Anna Livia Plurabelle, the mother-river personifying the Liffey, surfaces here amid the burial of the giant in the landscape, the archaeological mound, the Four Annalists surveying history. In this Age of Gods (transition) passage, her feminine current of forgiveness and renewal flows through the dream landscape, carrying Dublin's history from source to sea.
